notes: §1985:VI.6.8.4 GR3: "The COMPUTE statement allows the user to combine arithmetic operations without the restrictions on composite of operands and/or receiving data items imposed by the arithmetic statements ADD, SUBTRACT, MULTIPLY, and DIVIDE" and "each implementor will indicate the techniques used in handling arithmetic expressions". The 18-digit composite cap of §1985:VI.6.4.4 is CheckComposite (cap = the edition's MaxDigits, 18 at 85), which only the ADD, SUBTRACT, MULTIPLY, DIVIDE and CORRESPONDING binders call; BindCompute binds the expression and every receiver without calling it, at every edition, and EmitCompute evaluates the expression once in the implementor's documented technique (docs/CONFORMANCE.md row DOC-A.1-123: a scaled Int128 intermediate, exact wide form past it), which is the indication the second sentence asks for. Probed at 85: the witness's operands (9(10) and V9(10), composite 20) draw COBOL0805 in ADD A B GIVING R and compile in COMPUTE (5.5); COMPUTE R1 R2 = A + B with 9(18) and V9(18) operands and receivers (composite 36) and (A * B) / A + C store the exact values. The witness runs the 20-digit composite through COMPUTE.

next.reason: The freedom from composite-of-operands and receiving-item limits is kept: 'Arithmetic expressions allow the user to combine arithmetic operations without the restrictions on composite of operands and receiving data items' (§2023:8.8.1.2 GR7). With no ARITHMETIC clause 'it is as if the ARITHMETIC clause were specified with the NATIVE phrase' (§2023:11.9.5.2 GR4), and then 'the techniques used in handling arithmetic expressions and intrinsic functions shall be those specified by the implementor' (§2023:11.9.5.2 GR1), so 1985's implementor-chosen technique survives for a 1985 program. It is no longer unrestricted: under native arithmetic a COMPUTE whose expression is a single fixed-point literal or data item 'evaluates to the exact algebraic value of that literal or item' (§2023:14.9.8.4 GR1), a requirement 1985 left to the implementor. The requirement is stricter.
